label: Scully builds a lathe
detail: John J. Scully builds a weight-driven disc lathe.

label: Neumann AM31
detail: Neumann's first lathe, the AM31, arrives.

label: Ortofon cutter head
detail: Ortofon makes its first moving-coil cutter head.

label: The hot stylus
detail: William S. Bachman at Columbia develops the heated cutting stylus.

label: Variable pitch at Scully
detail: Per Wikipedia, Scully introduces variable pitch, automated in 1955.

label: RIAA curve standardized
detail: The RIAA equalization curve replaces a mix of competing EQs, after the 1953 NARTB standard.

label: 45/45 stereo cutter head
detail: Per Wikipedia, Western Electric/Westrex demonstrates the first commercial 45/45 stereo cutter head.

label: Neumann VMS 70
detail: Neumann's VMS 70, which Pspatial Audio calls the world's most popular recording lathe.

label: IEC adds a fourth time constant
detail: The IEC adds a 7950 microsecond infrasonic roll-off to the RIAA curve.

label: Neumann VMS 80
detail: Neumann's last lathe line, the first without the traditional bed, with DC servo motors.

label: Last VMS-82 DMM lathe
detail: The last Neumann VMS-82 DMM lathe is assembled in Berlin.

label: US loses its last DMM room
detail: Per Wikipedia, the last public DMM facility in the US closes.

label: Lacquer factory fire
detail: A fire destroys the Apollo Masters lacquer factory in Banning, California, leaving MDC in Japan as the sole lacquer maker.

label: Agnew Type 612
detail: A new disk mastering lathe is unveiled at the International Disk Recording and Mastering Convention.

label: APC-2 lathe
detail: MusicTech reports the Teenage Engineering and SUPERSENSE APC-2, a 104 kg made-to-order lathe.
